brief.topic: A Spiral That Grows Without Forgetting Its Shape

s01: This spiral grows without forgetting its shape.
Each quarter turn makes the distance from its center one and a half times larger.
The rule keeps multiplying as the curve turns.
Start at this small radius.
After one quarter turn, it has grown by the same factor.
After the next quarter turn, multiply again.
The added distance gets larger, but the proportion stays the same.
Now follow the direction of the curve.
Compare it with the direction pointing away from the center.
The angle between them stays constant.
The spiral is always making the same kind of turn, wherever we look.
Enlarge a copy by that growth factor.
Rotate it by a quarter turn.
The overlapping part fits the original curve.
What looked like a new scale is the same relationship appearing again.
This family is called logarithmic spirals.
Different growth factors make tighter or more open curves.
No single factor is required, and this one is not the golden spiral.
Living shapes can resemble these curves without following them exactly.
The beauty here is a rule of growth: keep changing size, and keep a relationship intact.

scenes.narration:
This spiral grows without forgetting its shape. Each quarter turn makes the distance from its center one and a half times larger. The rule keeps multiplying as the curve turns.

Start at this small radius. After one quarter turn, it has grown by the same factor. After the next quarter turn, multiply again. The added distance gets larger, but the proportion stays the same.

Now follow the direction of the curve. Compare it with the direction pointing away from the center. The angle between them stays constant. The spiral is always making the same kind of turn, wherever we look.

Enlarge a copy by that growth factor. Rotate it by a quarter turn. The overlapping part fits the original curve. What looked like a new scale is the same relationship appearing again.

This family is called logarithmic spirals. Different growth factors make tighter or more open curves. No single factor is required, and this one is not the golden spiral. Living shapes can resemble these curves without following them exactly. The beauty here is a rule of growth: keep changing size, and keep a relationship intact.
